newsitem.title: FRANCE: Europe envoy sees possible "pressure" on Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Europe envoy sees possible "pressure" on Netanyahu.

text.p: Europe's Middle East envoy said on Friday that mediators were still giving diplomacy a chance but that pressure could be applied on Israel to save the faltering peace process.
"There is great tension now. It is one of the most difficult times since the Madrid peace conference," ambassador Miguel Moratinos told France's Europe-1 radio in an interview from Dubai.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem "has broken the confidence which existed between Israelis and Palestinians...It's a political error," Moratinos said.
Asked what the European Union would do if Netanyahu went on building settlements, the envoy answered: "We are still giving diplomacy a chance, we are all making very intense efforts.
"There will be important meetings this weekend next week and I think we can all arrive at establishing (a form of) pressure to try and avoid this situation," Moratinos said, without elaborating.
Meetings due next week include Netanyahu's with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Washington on Monday.
Clashes have flared daily in the West Bank since Israel broke ground for 6,500 homes for Jews on the pine-covered Jerusalem hill on the road to Bethlehem two weeks ago.
Palestinians insist peace talks can restart only when Israel halts work on the settlement. REUTER
